sections.label: The opening
sections.line: How a vault acts like a database on a server that cannot read anything.
sections.para: Everything is encrypted on the client, so a fully compromised server leaks nothing confidential. A client computes the name of the one mutable file, the ref, from the read key; then commit, tree and file follow in about four requests. Every other object is named by its ciphertext's hash, verifiable without a key and cacheable for ever. Vaults go on web pages file by file, or as apps in a sandboxed frame with a narrow sg bridge.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: No leak on compromise, one key-derived mutable file, immutable objects, four requests, two web modes.
sections.para: Behaviour policies are the next layer for vault apps.

sections.label: The principle
sections.line: If the server failed completely and someone had all of it, nothing confidential would leak.
sections.para: No contents, names or readable structure, and no way to link objects to files.

sections.label: Making it act like a database
sections.line: Git is a database of objects; here the server can read neither objects nor pointers.
sections.para: One vault key decrypts everything; the read key reads but cannot write and can be published.

sections.label: The deterministic file
sections.line: The ref's name is an HMAC of the read key over a fixed domain and the vault id.
sections.para: It is the only derived and mutable file, ref-pid-muw, updated by compare-and-swap, holding the head commit id.

sections.label: The walk
sections.line: Ref, commit, tree, file: three or four plain GETs, decrypted in the browser.
sections.para: Any storage that answers a GET can serve the read half.

sections.label: Immutable, and named by its content
sections.line: Every other object is obj-cas-imm, named by the SHA-256 of its ciphertext.
sections.para: Verifiable with no key, cacheable for ever, and tamper-evident through the parent chain.

sections.label: One file to refresh a whole site
sections.line: Re-read one file, the ref; if unchanged, every cached object is still right.
sections.para: A documentation site can be built from a vault and updated by updating the vault.

sections.label: Two ways onto a web page
sections.line: File by file, or an HTML app in a sandboxed frame that can only ask the host through sg.
sections.para: The host holds the key and checks each request against declared permissions, denied by default.

sections.label: Next: behaviour policies for vault apps
sections.line: The app permission model is already a small policy; writing it as a behaviour policy adds purpose.
sections.para: As the teacher's vault tutor is sent one lesson and nothing else.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: From sgit-ai 0.21.0's code; ids 12 or 32 hex; metadata still visible to the server.
sections.para: The bridge API's reference is the SG/Send project's.

sections.line: The editor's explanation and the sgit-ai package's code.
